page: Amazon Web Services m5dn.metal is a bare-metal, general-purpose server instance powered by two dedicated Intel Xeon 8259CL processors. It features 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz, supported by 384 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 3,600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. The architecture is x86_64, utilizing hyper-threading and advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AES for cryptographic operations.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 81,985.6 and a Passmark CPU score of 56,892.01, placing it in the top 25% tier. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 4,542.21 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 95.59 GB/sec. Database operations and key-value store performance are also notable, with Redis SET operations reaching 77.66 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring 21,840.94.

While the instance excels in high-throughput network tasks, database operations, and static web serving, it exhibits limitations in machine learning text generation. LLM inference text generation speeds for both small and medium models fall into the bottom 10% tier due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. Consequently, this server is best suited for high-performance databases, memory-intensive general-purpose applications, high-throughput web serving, and network-bound workloads rather than deep learning or LLM text generation.
description: Amazon Web Services m5dn.metal is a bare-metal, general-purpose server equipped with 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores) via Intel Xeon 8259CL processors running at 3.1 GHz. It features 384 GB of DDR4 memory, 3,600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks show strong multi-core performance (stress-ng multi-core score of 81,985.6) and high memory bandwidth, alongside strong database execution capabilities, such as 77.66 million Redis SET operations per second. However, without GPU acceleration, it performs poorly in LLM text generation tasks. This instance is highly cost-efficient for resource-dense, network-heavy, and storage-intensive workloads, making it ideal for large-scale databases, high-throughput web serving, and enterprise general-purpose applications.
